requirement:
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.

An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
## Judgment

`requirements.references.anchors` is implemented and marked completely, and the tests cover its main cases and failure paths. I found no gaps and no FIXME comments. I did not run the tests; this judgment rests on reading the code and test assertions.

## Implementation

Each obligation maps to marked code:

- **Option syntax and placement.**
  - `definition_blocks` in `src/lib.rs` reads option lines only on consecutive lines immediately after the opening fence, and not for `{definition}` terms.
  - `option_line` parses `:name: value`, one per line.
  - `DefinitionBlock` and `DefinitionOption` carry the options.
- **Allowed options and errors.** `collect_definitions` in `src/evidence.rs` accepts `:impl:` only on a `{req}` and `:test:` on a `{req}` or `{example}`. Any other option is a validation error ("unsupported option"), and so is an empty value.
- **Impl/test edges.** `Anchor` (kind, file, selector) and `Declaration.anchors` represent the edge, and `Anchor::parse` splits `path#selector`. `Anchor::resolve` resolves through `OutlineCache::parse` and `ParsedSource::resolve`. That path applies project containment and permission rules via `resolve_evidence_file`/`check_project_file` (the `requirements.ci.input_containment` machinery that `requirements.ci.schema` points to). The empty selector selects the root node.
- **Option lines stay out of text and rendering.**
  - `without_options` strips them from the definition text, so `Declaration.text` and `raw_lines` (the requirements input) exclude them.
  - `preprocess_book` also uses `without_options`.
  - `replace_definitions` renders from `text_start`, which skips them.
- **Coverage.** `validate_references` requires an outline input that selects the anchored node or one of its ancestors, which includes the root node. Otherwise it reports "no input selects … anchored by :impl: …". Because that input records the node's hash, changing the file makes the evidence stale.
- **Unresolvable anchors.**
  - CI validation reports `:impl: anchor <path> on requirement <name> at <decl> does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node`, naming the definition and the path.
  - `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` checks access and resolution before inference. It fails with `<name>: cannot read :impl: anchor <path>`, and a denied path aborts with `PermissionDenied`.
  - Anchors feed mandatory inputs through `Anchor::selector`.
  - Under `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, an anchor under default-excluded `evidence/` is omitted rather than reported; that is a deliberate exception.
- **Other surfaces.** The `references` tool in `src/authoring/tools.rs` reports anchors as lineless sites, with a node selector when one is given. `DefinitionEdges::current` in `src/index.rs` uses anchors to group detail-page inputs. Both are marked `{impl}`.
- **Skill direction.** The `{req}` declaration itself carries `:impl: assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`. That skill's "Authoring format" section explains anchors and says "Do not anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such as a comment attached to the Rust item…". The bootstrap skill defers to the requirements skill for directive syntax, so the bundle as a whole gives the direction.

The other behavior in the marked code is specified by other definitions: the reference-set digest by `ci.reference_set`, input grouping by `index.detail_format`, and generated-evidence omission by `authoring.mandatory_inputs`.

## Tests

- `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` (`src/evidence.rs`):
  - Option lines are excluded from the text, so no "text changed" error appears.
  - A section-only input does not cover a whole-file anchor.
  - A missing `:test:` path gives the "does not resolve" error naming the definition and path.
  - A root-node input passes.
  - Editing the anchored file makes the evidence stale.
  - A `:test:` anchor on an example passes.
- `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers three cases:
  - A sibling node does not cover the anchor.
  - The node itself, its parent and the root each cover it.
  - A bad selector reports "no outline node matches".
- `unsupported_and_empty_options_are_validation_errors` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers an unknown option, an empty value, and `:impl:` on an example.
- `requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines` (`src/evidence.rs`) and `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` (`src/lib.rs`) cover:
  - Parsing the anchors.
  - Excluding option lines from `text`, `raw_lines`, and rendered output.
  - Treating `:impl:`/`:test:` lines that are not immediately after the fence as ordinary text.
  - Anchors on a requirement nested inside another requirement.
- `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs`, `unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference`, and `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`) cover:
  - Root and node anchors as mandatory inputs.
  - A missing file failing before inference.
  - A `habeas.toml` disallow giving `PermissionDenied`.
- `references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites` (`src/authoring/tools.rs`) covers anchor sites for a file and a node, and omission of a disallowed anchor.
- The `src/index.rs` and `src/lib.rs` tests cover anchor-based input grouping and the absence of `:impl:` from detail pages.

I did not find a CI-side test that a disallowed (rather than missing) anchor is reported as a validation error. That path goes through the same `resolve_evidence_file` code, so I do not treat it as a gap.

:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references: discovery MUST skip `.git` and `target` directories at any depth and the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories.
A source item MUST choose its references for each candidate definition by this
procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. If the item is a test or test helper designed to verify the definition, it
MUST use `{test}`.
2. Otherwise, if fulfilling the definition depends on the item, it MUST use
`{impl}`. For code, this means it makes a decision, performs a check,
produces an output, or handles a case the definition specifies. For a type,
this means the definition constrains its shape: fields, variants, serialized
form, or validation.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
4. If the item carries no reference after applying steps 1 to 3 to every
definition, it MUST cite the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, justifying why the item
exists.

:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, `references`, and `inputs`. `references` MUST be the reference-set digest defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} evidence_coverage

For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
